name: Kusunda
world_status: accessible description is silent on stress

sources.citation: Watters, David E. (with Yogendra P. Yadava, Madhav P. Pokharel, Balaram Prasain). 2006. Notes on Kusunda Grammar: A language isolate of Nepal. Himalayan Linguistics Archive 3, pp. 1-182 (first ed. 2005, NFDIN, Kathmandu). DOI 10.5070/H90023671,https://escholarship.org/uc/item/83v8d1wv
sources.note: Ch. 4 Phonology (pp. 22-43) has no stress/accent/suprasegmental section and never states where stress falls; the only stress mention is a passing remark on p. 32 (§4.4.1) that the p/b voicing contrast is sometimes neutralized intervocalically 'especially in rapid speech and if the syllable in question is unstressed'. Pitch is discussed only as a concomitant lowering under pharyngealization before voiced uvulars (§4.3.2, p. 26) and as falling-rising pitch on the negative suffix -aˤu (§5.5.4.1, §6.1.2.2).

sources.locator: printed pp. 20 (§3 Linguistic type), 22 (§4 Phonology intro), 26–27 (§4.3.2 Pharyngealization of vowels and lowering of pitch), 32 (§4.4.1), 41, 72 (§5.5.4.1),…
sources.note: No catalog entry for kusu1250. The work never states a word-stress or tone system: 'stress', 'accent', 'tone', 'tonal' do not occur as topics (the only stress token is the incidental 'unstressed' on p. 32; 'tone' occurs only in 'overtones'). sources.citation: Reinhard, Johan & Sueyoshi Toba. 1970. A preliminary linguistic analysis and vocabulary of the Kusunda language. Kathmandu: Summer Institute of Linguistics and Tribhuvan University. 31 pp.
sources.note: The only other primary phonological sketch (SIL-style 'preliminary linguistic analysis' of the 1968-69 Dang-Deukhuri data); SIL sketches of this era routinely include a stress statement. Basis for van Driem 2001 and Spendley 2024.

sources.citation: Donohue, Mark. 2013. Kusunda phonology: Phonological structure ('Phonological notes' page of the Kusunda project website; team Mark Donohue, Bhojraj Gautam, Madhav P. Pokharel). Canberra: School of Language Studies / Linguistics, The Australian National University.http://kusunda.linguistics.anu.edu.au/phonology.php(page footer: 'Updated: 5 October 2013 / Responsible Officer: Mark Donohue'; live domain dead; Internet Archive captures 2013-04-10 to 2019-04-01).
sources.note: Donohue calls Kusunda 'segmentally uncomplicated and prosodically rich' and states that its suprasegmental system 'does not include pitch specification (i.e., a tone system)', which he flags as exceptional for a Himalayan language; the prosodies listed in the 'Kusunda prosodies' table are breathiness (formerly analysed as a breathy consonant series, but attested on onsetless syllables), pharyngealisation (after Watters, a regressive effect of the voiced uvulars) and nasalisation (recent), all freely co-occurring on one syllable; no tone or pitch row.
